# M1-5c: Slack status message (perpetually edited heartbeat)

- Milestone: M1
- Branch / worktree: `t/M1-5c`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M1-5c`
- Depends on: M1-5b (merged)
- Touches (exclusive while running): new `status/`; small wiring in `cmd/`, `config/`, `deploy/deploy.sh` (env keys
  only), `.env.example`; one small migration in `store/` (status message id)
- Plan refs: architecture.md §6 (N2). **Decision 2026-11-01 (Brendan):** instead of healthchecks.io, finbot keeps one
  status message in `#finbot-finances` that it edits after every sync. Brendan's own Slack automation alerts when it
  goes stale. Facts about the Slack app: docs/build/spikes/slack.md (F2: resolve the private channel id with
  `users.conversations?types=private_channel`; F3: `chat:write` covers post and update).
- YNAB access: read-only live (local check)
- Deploy: yes (sup re-runs `./deploy/deploy.sh`)

## Goal
After each sync tick (success, failure or skip) and each backup run, `finbot serve` edits a single status message in
`#finbot-finances` so its content and its "edited" time always reflect the latest state. Brendan pins it once by hand
(the bot has no `pins:write` scope and doesn't need it).

## Scope
1. **`status/`:** plain `net/http` calls to `chat.postMessage` and `chat.update` (no slack-go yet; that's M3).
   - find the channel: `SLACK_STATUS_CHANNEL` (default `finbot-finances`) by name via `users.conversations`
     (private channels), cached after the first lookup;
   - on first run (no stored message ts), post the message, store `channel_id` + `ts` in the store
     (new migration, a one-row table), and log "status message created; pin it in Slack";
   - afterwards `chat.update` that message. If Slack says `message_not_found` or `channel_not_found`, post a fresh one
     and store the new ts;
   - message content (plain mrkdwn, no ids, no amounts): overall state (OK / degraded / failing); last successful sync
     time (America/Denver); last error (redacted, one line); per-account newest import date with link-error flags
     (account names only); last backup time and result; import on/off; finbot version (git SHA);
   - rate: at most one update per sync tick plus one per backup run. Slack errors only log; they never fail a tick.
2. **Wiring (`cmd/`):** `serve` calls the status updater after each sync tick and each backup run. It's disabled, with a
   startup log line saying so, when `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` is empty. The token is scrubbed from all logs and errors.
3. **Timezone:** set `TZ=America/Denver` (hoid's zone) in `deploy/compose.yaml` so `BACKUP_AT` and status times are local; `tzdata` is already in the image.
4. **Version:** embed the git SHA at build time (`-ldflags -X`), passed by the Dockerfile from a build arg that
   `deploy.sh` sets from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
5. **Deploy:** `deploy.sh` adds `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and the optional `SLACK_STATUS_CHANNEL` to `finbot.env`, with the
   same stdin/0600 handling.

## Out of scope
- Socket Mode, questions, alerts, reports (M3). Pinning via the API. Any change to healthchecks ping code.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Unit tests with a fake Slack (`httptest`): first run posts and stores the ts; the next run updates the same ts;
      `message_not_found` → re-post; Slack 5xx → logged, tick unaffected; content has no UUIDs, amounts or token;
      disabled when the token is empty.
- [ ] Live, from the worktree with a temp DB (read-only YNAB): `SYNC_INTERVAL=1m ./finbot serve` for ~3 minutes posts
      one message in `#finbot-finances` and then edits it (show the Slack `edited` timestamp advancing via
      `conversations.history` for that ts; print only ts and edited.ts, not text). Then delete that test message with
      `chat.delete` so the deployed instance creates the real one. Secret grep of logs: 0.
- [ ] `docker build .` passes; `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green.
